Trapping the Center: A Journey into Geometric Probability

math
probability
geometry
What is the probability that \(n\) random points on a circle contain the center?
Author

Alex Shao

Published

December 18, 2025

Imagine you have a circular piece of plywood. You randomly hammer 6 nails into the very edge of the circle. If you wrap a rubber band around those nails, what are the odds that the center of the wood is trapped inside that rubber band?

This is a classic problem in the field of geometric probability. The idea was taken from a youtube video I found online, but can also be found here along with a selection of other super fun puzzles.

Anyway, I’ve attached an interactive version of this puzzle. Feel free to play around with it however you like.

//| echo: false // This is an Observable JS cell in Quarto viewof nPoints = Inputs.range([3, 12], {value: 6, step: 1, label: “Number of Points (n)”})

canvas = { const width = 400; const height = 400; const context = DOM.context2d(width, height); const radius = 150; const center = { x: width / 2, y: height / 2 };

// Generate random points on the circumference const points = Array.from({ length: nPoints }, () => { const angle = Math.random() * Math.PI * 2; return { x: center.x + radius * Math.cos(angle), y: center.y + radius * Math.sin(angle), angle: angle }; }).sort((a, b) => a.angle - b.angle);

// Logic: Check if center (0,0) is inside // A point is inside if all consecutive points form a gap < PI let isInside = true; for (let i = 0; i < points.length; i++) { const nextIdx = (i + 1) % points.length; let gap = points[nextIdx].angle - points[i].angle; if (gap < 0) gap += Math.PI * 2; if (gap > Math.PI) isInside = false; }

// Drawing context.clearRect(0, 0, width, height);

// Draw Circle context.beginPath(); context.arc(center.x, center.y, radius, 0, Math.PI * 2); context.strokeStyle = “#ccc”; context.stroke();

// Draw Polygon context.beginPath(); context.moveTo(points[0].x, points[0].y); points.forEach(p => context.lineTo(p.x, p.y)); context.closePath(); context.fillStyle = isInside ? “rgba(76, 175, 80, 0.3)” : “rgba(244, 67, 54, 0.3)”; context.fill(); context.strokeStyle = isInside ? “#4CAF50” : “#F44336”; context.stroke();

// Draw Center context.beginPath(); context.arc(center.x, center.y, 4, 0, Math.PI * 2); context.fillStyle = “black”; context.fill();

return context.canvas; }

Introduction

\[ \cos(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n x^{2n}}{(2n)!} = 1 - \frac{x^2}{2!} + \frac{x^4}{4!} - \cdots \]

Applications

Taylor series are used in:

  1. Numerical approximations - Computing values of transcendental functions
  2. Physics - Linearizing equations near equilibrium points

Visual Example

Consider approximating \(e^x\) near \(x = 0\):

Order Approximation Value at \(x=1\)
0 \(1\) 1.000
1 \(1 + x\) 2.000
2 \(1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2}\) 2.500
3 \(1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2} + \frac{x^3}{6}\) 2.667
∞ \(e^x\) 2.718…
